items.headline: Court lets custody death family view CCTV
items.text: The Madras High Court on 20 Nov let lorry driver R Balakrishnan's family view CCTV from four police stations on 23 Nov. Police say he died by suicide in custody; the state opposed releasing footage.

photo.alt: A city of low buildings and trees with four tall carved temple towers rising above the rooftops.
photo.caption: Madurai, with the towers of the Meenakshi temple, in 2006. File photo of the city.

items.headline: Court drops UAPA charges against Kerala journalist
items.text: A Nagpur court dropped UAPA charges against journalist Rejaz M Sheeba Sydeek, jailed 560 days over alleged Maoist links, but framed charges under BNS section 152. His bail hearing is on 3 Dec.

photo.alt: A tall pale-yellow office building behind trees and street lamps, with motorbikes and cars on the road in front.
photo.caption: The District Court building in Nagpur, in 2011. File photo.

items.figcap: personnel at his home, he said
items.headline: Leh police lift guard at Wangchuk's home
items.text: Leh police on 20 Nov withdrew personnel enforcing a prohibitory order on activist Sonam Wangchuk, who said 20–25 armed personnel had confined him since 11 Nov. Police say he was never under house arrest.

photo.alt: A street of shops under strings of prayer flags, with people walking and cars parked; a man in maroon robes in the foreground.
photo.caption: A street in Leh, Ladakh, in 2007. File photo of the town.

items.headline: Railway demolition of 101 Mumbai homes halted
items.text: Western Railway halted demolition of 101 homes on its land near Prabhadevi station on 20 Nov after protests and state intervention. It will wait for a 26 Nov court hearing; rehabilitation is being planned.

photo.alt: Railway tracks and a long platform with commuters, overhead wires and a footbridge, with tall towers behind.
photo.caption: Prabhadevi railway station, Mumbai, in 2025. File photo of the area.

items.place: Kaja and Katcha, Buram, South Kordofan, Sudan
items.headline: Drone strikes kill seven in South Kordofan villages
items.text: Drone strikes on two Buram villages on 19 Nov killed three children at a water pump and four farmers, Radio Tamazuj reported. Activists blamed the army; no army comment was reported.

photo.alt: An open dirt yard with storage containers, a truck and low buildings under a hazy sky.
photo.caption: A yard with storage buildings in Kadugli, capital of South Kordofan, in 2009. File photo of the state.

items.place: Bureij, Deir al-Balah and Nuseirat, central Gaza
items.headline: Strikes kill six to seven in central Gaza
items.text: Israeli strikes on 20 Nov killed six people in central Gaza, four near Bureij camp, Gaza's civil defence said; Anadolu, citing medics, counted seven. Israel's military said it targeted "multiple military operatives".

photo.alt: Palm groves and green fields with low houses, and more buildings on the horizon.
photo.caption: Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, in 2008. File photo of the area.

items.headline: Record settler attacks during West Bank olive harvest
items.text: UN agencies and aid groups said on 20 Nov that settlers carried out over 400 attacks during this olive harvest, more than any season before, damaging over 4,000 trees. No Israeli response was reported.

photo.alt: A gloved hand picking purple olives from a branch.
photo.caption: Olive picking near Dura in the Hebron governorate, southern West Bank.
photo.credit: M sh شراونة محمد / Wikimedia Commons

items.headline: Amnesty: Spanish police used excessive force at strike
items.text: Amnesty said police used batons, pepper spray and rubber bullets against protesters and journalists in the 11 Nov general strike, injuring 36. The Interior Ministry has curbed pepper spray; Madrid police opened an internal inquiry.

photo.alt: Marchers at night hold a long white banner reading 'Bloque Crítico por la huelga general'.
photo.caption: A general-strike march in Madrid on 14 November 2012, Spain's last general strike before this one.

items.headline: France passes law presuming police shootings lawful
items.text: France's Senate gave final approval on 20 Nov to a law presuming officers who fire their weapons act lawfully. Critics say it will hinder victims' families; the government says it protects officers in dangerous conditions.

photo.alt: A long cream stone palace with a central dome and clock, behind a green lawn under a blue sky.
photo.caption: The Luxembourg Palace in Paris, seat of the French Senate, in 2014. File photo.

focus.title: Palestine: Gaza and the West Bank
focus.dek: UN agencies counted 400+ settler attacks in this West Bank olive harvest, a record. Israeli strikes killed six to seven in central Gaza on 20 Nov.
